text.title: RACI AI Assisted Worked Examples
text.summary: One complete `RACIMatrix` refreshed on a roster delta (the security lead leaves, an appsec lead joins) with a note on every non-obvious value, and one bad matrix showing what the validator prints and what the PM sees beyond it.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: The checkout project has two open WBS leaves under 2 (Backend): 2.1 Login endpoint and 2.2 Rate limiting. The matrix was first published at kickoff on 2026-02-03. On 2026-05-08 HR posts that the security lead (dana.r) leaves on 2026-05-15 and that an appsec lead (maksym.d) has joined and taken over the security review. The PM (olena.k) runs the methodology with `trigger: roster_delta`; the deadline is the departing person's last day.

example.title: checkout RACIMatrix 1.4.0, roster delta refreshed on 2026-05-10
example.note: `roster` no longer contains `security-lead`: the snapshot is the roster as of `last_reviewed`, so any row still naming it would be `orphaned` and block publish (r-responsible-in-roster).
Two rows for two open leaves and none for `2`; a "2 Backend" row would hide an unowned 2.3 the day it is added to the WBS (r-rows-bind-to-wbs-leaves).

`accountable` is the same role on both rows, which is fine; what is forbidden is two roles on one row. The anchors are `charter#auth-scope` for 2.1 (the charter names the backend lead for authentication) and `wbs-dict#2.2` for 2.2 (the dictionary entry names the owner); both rows are `anchored`, so `status: published` is allowed (r-exactly-one-accountable-per-row, r-evidence-anchor-per-assignment).

`appsec-lead` is in C on 2.1 (asked before the login design is decided) and in I on 2.2 (told when rate limits ship), never in both on one row; C is not longer than R on any row, so no `over_consultation_reviewed` flag is needed (r-one-column-per-role-per-row).

`refresh_deadline` equals `effective_date` because the change is a leave; `last_reviewed` 2026-05-10 is five days before it. The reassignments carry `stakeholders#appsec-lead` as the anchor for the new role (r-trigger-enum-and-roster-delta).

The 2026-05-10 publish entry notifies exactly the roles holding R or A (`backend-lead`, `backend-engineer`) with their rows; `pm` and `appsec-lead` hold only C / I and are not required recipients (r-notify-assignees-on-publish).
`last_reviewed` is well inside 90 days of the review date; `scripts/staleness-check.py` on the weekly cron would print `FRESH` (r-quarterly-review-90-days).

example.title: What the validator and the PM reject
example.note: Validator output: `$.rows[0].accountable: 'backend-lead, pm' does not match pattern '^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$'`, `$.rows[0].evidence: 0 items, minItems=1`, `$.rows[1].status: must equal 'anchored', got 'proposed'`, `$.roster_delta: missing required field`, `$.review_log[0].notification: missing required field`.

Once those schema errors are fixed, the cross-field block reports the rest: `rows: open WBS leaf 2.2 has no row (r-rows-bind-to-wbs-leaves)`, `rows: 2 is a summary node (parent of another row); only leaves get rows (r-rows-bind-to-wbs-leaves)`, `rows[0]: role 'pm' in both consulted and informed (r-one-column-per-role-per-row)`, `rows[0]: roles ['security-lead'] not in roster and row not 'orphaned' (r-responsible-in-roster)`, `rows[0]: consulted (2) longer than responsible (1) and not reviewed by the PM (r-one-column-per-role-per-row)`, `rows[1]: roles ['security-lead'] not in roster and row not 'orphaned' (r-responsible-in-roster)`.

What the PM sees beyond the validator: the model hedged on the row where the charter was silent and named both leads, which is the row where nobody will run the security review; `security-lead` left on 2026-05-15 and the matrix says nothing about who took the consultation, so the login design goes out unreviewed; and "published" with no notification means the backend engineer learns about 2.2 in the incident review.
